subject: Hosting preference & SOC2/BAA evidence — next steps (PulseMed)
messages:
From: Tessa Morgan <tessa.morgan@redwood.com>
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@pulsemed.com>, Maya Singh <maya.singh@pulsemed.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-demo recap + hosting/evidence checklist (PulseMed)

Hi Daniel and Maya —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we can narrow the hosting path and get procurement moving:

Summary of constraints you mentioned on the call:
- PHI in downstream results (brief patient identifiers may be present) — so HIPAA applies.
- Internal security wants an auditable BAA + SOC 2 Type II evidence for the inference stack.
- Prefer private network isolation but open to Dedicated if contractually equivalent (BAA + VPC-level isolation).

What we need to qualify the hosting mode and produce an MAA (mutual action plan):
1) Primary hosting preference: Hosted API vs Dedicated reservation vs Private (VPC/on-prem). If you have a strict preference for VPC/on-prem, let us know why (network controls, audit timeline, data residency).
2) Scope of PHI and endpoints that will call Redwood (numbers and which services: embeddings, chat, bulk batch inference).
3) SOC2 evidence recipients — do you require the full SOC2 report or a summary + vendor attestation?
4) Any additional audit artifacts (encryption key management details, retention policy, access controls) you need up front.

Attached are two items to speed review: a one-page SOC2 summary and a short template MAA we can adapt.
[Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_summary.pdf] [Attachment: MAA_pulsemed.docx]

Proposed next steps (feel free to edit):
- PulseMed confirms hosting preference and evidence recipients (by Wed 10/6).
- We return a tailored MAA and a timeline for Dedicated/Private onboarding (emailed 10/7).
- If Privately-hosted: schedule security scoping call with infra (Karthik) week of 10/11.

Karthik and Sean are on copy — Karthik will own the technical scoping, Sean will coordinate legal/procurement artifacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

Best,
Tessa Morgan
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[redwood.com]

Tessa —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our security/legal side after reviewing the SOC2 summary:

1) Hosting preference: Our security team leans toward Private VPC (customer-managed VPC peering) because of network egress controls and our internal audit schedule in November. We could consider Dedicated only if you can confirm: (a) a formal BAA, (b) VPC-level isolation that meets our IP allowlist requirements, and (c) a guaranteed maintenance window with advance notice.

2) Evidence: For procurement to move, we will need a redacted SOC2 Type II full report (vendor-provided) and the BAA executed with Redwood. The SOC2 summary is helpful but not sufficient for legal — redacted report + SOC2 letter + auditor name.

3) Scope: Initial integration will be real-time embeddings + reranking API; throughput small to start (under 10 req/s), but we expect rapid growth after pilot.

4) Timeline: If you can provide the redacted SOC2 report and a draft BAA by 10/7, we can schedule an internal security review 10/11–10/12 and aim to finalize procurement by end of October.

I've attached our vendor security questionnaire — some of the fields are quick, some will need answers from your infra/security team.
[Attachment: PulseMed_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx]

Thanks — Daniel
Director, Engineering — PulseMed

Date: Mon, 04 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo recap + hosting/evidence checklist (PulseMed)

Hi Daniel / Maya —

Karthik from Redwood infra — thanks for the notes and the questionnaire. I went through PulseMed_Security_Questionnaire.xlsx and pulled answers for the high-impact items you flagged. Below are concise responses; we can expand any bullets into a technical appendix if you prefer.

1) BAA / SOC2
- BAA: Redwood executes BAAs with customers handling PHI. I'll attach a draft MAA that includes the BAA as Exhibit A — if PulseMed legal prefers a separate BAA we can do that too.
- SOC2: We can provide a redacted SOC2 Type II report and an SOC2 letter with the auditor name. I'll share the redacted PDF by end of day 10/07.

2) Hosting options and what each provides (short):
- Hosted API: fastest onboarding but not recommended for PHI in your case unless you accept additional safeguards and a BAA; network isolation limited.
- Dedicated: single-tenant GPU pool, VPC peering, and IP allowlist. We can include BAA and an SLA. Typical lead for Dedicated (BAA in place) is ~3–4 weeks after contract execution for a small pool.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): full network isolation and control, supported via customer-managed VPC peering or on-prem package. On-prem (air-gapped) timelines vary (4–8 weeks + infra coordination).

3) Key audit questions you asked
- KMS / key handling: We support customer-managed CMEK via KMIP/KMS integrations for Private and Dedicated via HSM-backed KMS. Hosted API uses Redwood-managed KMS by default but can integrate with customer KMS in Dedicated/Private.
- Data retention / logs: We provide configurable retention windows and exportable audit logs (S3-style exports). Logs are stored encrypted at rest.
- Access controls: RBAC + SCIM for enterprise SSO; privileged access reviews monthly.

4) Proposed mutual action plan (dates are provisional):
- 10/07: Redwood sends redacted SOC2 + draft BAA and updated MAA (Tessa ownership).
- 10/11: PulseMed security review (you).
- 10/13: Technical scoping call (Karthik + PulseMed infra) to confirm VPC peering details and KMS approach.
- 10/20: If Dedicated chosen, draft contract for Dedicated capacity and SOW.

Attachments I will supply: Redwood redacted SOC2 (10/7), updated MAA/BAA draft (10/7). Also linking the internal onboarding playbook for VPC peering (internal link): https://redwood.app/internal/vpc-onboarding (we'll send a shareable version to your infra during scoping).

If PulseMed wants to accelerate, we can swap the order: sign BAA earlier to start Dedicated provisioning in parallel with the security review.

Happy to jump on a call tomorrow morning if that's useful.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
